note: 'Abraham stepped forward and said, Will You really sweep away the righteous with the wicked?' (Gen 18:23), and down through fifty, forty-five, forty, thirty, twenty, ten. Closed at 18:33: 'When the LORD had finished speaking with Abraham, He departed'.; "called on the name of the LORD"

'the cave at Machpelah in the field near Mamre, which Abraham had purchased from Ephron the Hittite as a burial site' (Gen 50:13) -- the purchase recalled two generations later, as the reason Jacob could be buried there. Genesis 23:16 is the sale itself, four hundred shekels weighed out.; 'weighed out for him the price he had named ... four hundred shekels of silver, according to the standard of the merchants' (Gen 23:16), and the field, the cave and all the trees 'deeded by the Hittites to Abraham' (Gen 23:17-20). The first ground he owned in the land he was promised, bought to bury Sarah in, and afterwards the tomb of Abraham, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob and Leah.
'Abraham said to his servant, the elder ... will go to my country and my kindred to take a wife for my son Isaac' (Gen 24:2-4), under an oath sworn hand-under-thigh.

'I am the God of your father Abraham. Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham' (Gen 26:24). **The title is God's own**, spoken to Isaac about a man already dead, and it is the reason given for the blessing on the son.
'and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite' (Gen 26:34), taken with Judith in the same verse.
'When Esau was forty years old, he took as his wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite' (Gen 26:34).

'Then the LORD appeared to Abraham by the Oaks of Mamre' (Gen 18:1). The verse says 'him'; Abraham is named at 18:13, 'And the LORD asked Abraham', which is the same scene and the same speaker.; "the LORD appeared to Abram"

'Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your descendants for the sake of My servant Abraham' (Gen 26:24). The verse says 'you'; Isaac is named through the chapter and at 26:12, 'Now Isaac sowed seed in the land ... And the LORD blessed him'.; God blessed his son Isaac
'They carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave at Machpelah in the field' (Gen 50:13). The verse says 'him'; the chapter names him at 50:2, 'the physicians embalmed Israel'.
'Joseph said to Pharaoh’s court ... let me go and bury my father' (Gen 50:4-5), answered at 50:6: 'Pharaoh replied, Go up and bury your father'.

'So Joseph died at the age of 110. And they embalmed his body and placed it in a coffin in Egypt.' (Gen 50:26), having dwelt there since 50:22.; Joseph died in Egypt (implied from 'placed it in a coffin in Egypt').
'indeed the sons of Machir son of Manasseh were brought up on Joseph’s knees' (Gen 50:23).
'I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah bore to Nahor.' (Gen 24:24), repeated by the servant at 24:47.; 'son of Milcah'
'Rebekah came out ... She was the daughter of Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Abraham’s brother Nahor' (Gen 24:15).; Nahor’s wife was named Milcah; 'the wife of Nahor'
'I am Abraham’s servant, he replied' (Gen 24:34) -- his own words, and the nearest the chapter comes to naming him.
'And he set out for Nahor's hometown in Aram-naharaim.' (Gen 24:10), with ten camels of his master's.
